The use of automated office blood pressure measurement (AOBPM) in primary care is feasible.

automated office blood pressure (AOBP) is a more accurate method than clinic blood pressure (CBP) to measure blood pressure in the office and that it is feasible to implement AOBP in a primary care practice.

automated office BP measurement is a valid and reliable alternative to manual office measurement in primary care, and that the use of an automated device is associated with a reduction of BP in the clinic and a decrease in BP variability.

the design, development and evaluation of an automated blood pressure measurement system.
developing a system to automatically measure blood pressure in an office setting, using an arm cuff.

the development and application of automated office blood pressure measurement techniques in primary care, and the use of this technique in the diagnosis of hypertension, and in the management and follow-up of hypertensive patients in primary care.

the automated blood pressure measurement in the office is not a reliable method of diagnosis and treatment of hypertension.
office blood pressure measurements should not be used for diagnosis, but should be used for treatment decisions.

automated blood pressure measurement in the office setting is an acceptable alternative to auscultatory blood pressure measurement for diagnosis of hypertension and for management of patients with hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
automated blood pressure measurement is a useful adjunct to office blood pressure measurement for the diagnosis, management and treatment of hypertension.
automated blood pressure measurement is a reliable method of measuring blood pressure in the primary care setting.
the use of automated office blood pressure (BP) measurement is a valuable and cost-effective method to detect hypertension and to guide therapy.

office BP measurement in primary care is feasible and accurate.
